courses.title: Introduction to Sociology
courses.description: Introduction to problems in the analysis of social structures and processes. Basic sociological concepts will be introduced and their application demonstrated in various areas of sociology. Credit will be granted for only one of SOCI 100 or both SOCI 101, SOCI 102.

courses.title: Social Interaction and Culture
courses.description: Culture, identity, social interaction, relationships and socialization. Credit will be granted for only one of SOCI 101 or SOCI 100.

courses.title: Inequality and Social Change
courses.description: Inequality, institutions, social structure and social change. Credit will be granted for only one of SOCI 102 or SOCI 100.

courses.title: Sociology of Family
courses.description: An introduction to contemporary family forms and relations.

courses.title: Ethnicity
courses.description: An introduction to the study of the relations between ethnic groups and of the interplay between ethnicity and other social factors.

courses.title: Global Population Dynamics
courses.description: Core processes that influence world population patterns and trends.

courses.title: Canadian Social Structure
courses.description: Descriptive and analytic survey of such features as demographic characteristics, class structure, ethnicity, and regional variation in Canadian society as a basis for understanding current social issues.

courses.title: Research Methods
courses.description: An introduction to sociological research methods. Diverse types of qualitative and quantitate data and methods to answer research questions. Prerequisite: One of SOCI 100, SOCI 101, SOCI 102, SOCI 200.

prereq.text: One of SOCI 100, SOCI 101, SOCI 102, SOCI 200

courses.title: Sociology of Indigenous Peoples
courses.description: Sociological perspective of Indigenous peoples and issues both internationally and within Canada.

courses.title: Sociology of Personal Life
courses.description: A sociological examination of everyday life exploring the social in the personal.

courses.title: Shopping, Society, and Sustainability
courses.description: Major theories of consumer society, evaluating impacts of shopping on human and non-human environments and popular solutions to these impacts.

courses.title: Introduction to Social Interaction
courses.description: Research on social interaction, with an emphasis on group (as opposed to individual) processes and behaviour.

courses.title: Crime and Society
courses.description: Crime as a social phenomenon, with emphasis on the changing definitions of crime in relation to social and political change in Canadian and other societies.

courses.title: Work, Technology, and Society
courses.description: Social forces responsible for changing patterns of technological innovation and work organization in modern industrial societies. Emphasis on the organization of work, labour force dynamics, and technological change.

courses.title: Sociology of Creativity
courses.description: The application of sociological concepts to the examination of creative processes.

courses.title: Data and Society
courses.description: Impacts of changing information and communication technologies on societies and social interactions.

courses.title: Health and Society
courses.description: An introduction to health and illness through a sociological lens.

courses.title: Citizenship and Identity
courses.description: The concepts of citizenship, identity, and human rights as social processes shaping individuals and communities (both local and global).

courses.title: Global Pandemics
courses.description: Global pandemics in relation to social inequality, social interaction and social institutions.

courses.title: Sociology of International Development
courses.description: Causes and consequences of uneven development in countries throughout the world. It is recommended that students complete one of SOCI 100, SOCI 101, or SOCI 102 before taking this course. Restricted to students with second-year standing or above.

courses.title: Ethnic and Racial Inequality
courses.description: A critical examination of classical and contemporary theories and research evidence concerning ethnic and racial inequality at the societal and interpersonal levels. It is recommended that students complete one of SOCI 100, SOCI 101, or SOCI 102 before taking this course. Restricted to students with second-year standing or above.

courses.title: Sociology of Migration
courses.description: Sociological approaches to the movement of peoples and its impact over time. It is recommended that students complete one of SOCI 100, SOCI 101, or SOCI 102 before taking this course. Restricted to students with second-year standing or above.

courses.title: Canadian Society
courses.description: Social organization of Canadian society: relationships between social institutions and social processes (e.g., economics, education, family, law, media, and politics); including issues of ancestry, ethnicity, gender, region, and social class. Prerequisite: One of SOCI 100, SOCI 101, SOCI 102.

courses.title: Gender Relations
courses.description: The nature of gender relations, their social and cultural expression, and theories of gender inequality. It is recommended that students complete one of SOCI 100, SOCI 101, or SOCI 102 before taking this course. Restricted to students with second-year standing or above.

courses.title: Sociology of Masculinity
courses.description: How masculinity differs across social contexts and time periods. It is recommended that students complete one of SOCI 100, SOCI 101, or SOCI 102 before taking this course. Restricted to students with second-year standing or above.

courses.title: Diversity in Family Forms
courses.description: An examination of diversity within and between families and of diverse family forms. It is recommended that students complete one of SOCI 100, SOCI 101, SOCI 102 or SOCI 200 before taking this course. Restricted to students with second-year standing or above.

courses.title: Sociology of the Life Course
courses.description: Individuals and families through the life course. It is recommended that students complete one of SOCI 100, SOCI 101, SOCI 102 or SOCI 200 before taking this course. Restricted to students with second-year standing or above.

courses.title: Social Statistics I
courses.description: The testing of sociological theories using quantitative data analysis techniques on numerical data from social surveys, experiments and official statistics. SOCI 328 excludes credit for a number of other statistics courses in various departments. Please consult the Science Credit Exclusion List ( https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/faculties-colleges-and-schools/faculty-science/bachelor-science/credit-exclusion-lists ) before registering. Prerequisite: One of SOCI 100, SOCI 101, SOCI 102.

courses.title: Sociology of Adornment
courses.description: The application of sociological concepts to the understanding of objects that we use to adorn our bodies. It is recommended that students complete one of SOCI 100, SOCI 101, or SOCI 102 before taking this course. Restricted to students with second-year standing or above.

courses.title: Consumers and Consumption
courses.description: The structure and culture of consuming and consumption. It is recommended that students complete one of SOCI 100, SOCI 101, or SOCI 102 before taking this course. Restricted to students with second-year standing or above.

courses.title: Sociology of Aging
courses.description: Demographic, economic, and social trends associated with aging, ageism, and aging populations. It is recommended that students complete one of SOCI 100, SOCI 101, SOCI 102 or SOCI 200 before taking this course. Credit will be granted for only one of SOCI 344 and SOCI 444. Equivalency: SOCI 444. Restricted to students with second-year standing or above.
courses.equivalency: SOCI 444. Restricted to students with second-year standing or above

courses.title: Work and Inequality
courses.description: The meaning of work and leisure, properties of work organization, the division of labour, and the relation of work and social inequality. It is recommended that students complete one of SOCI 100, SOCI 101, or SOCI 102 before taking this course. Restricted to students with second-year standing or above.

courses.title: Community Studies
courses.description: Study of the organization of human communities; a focus upon collective activities including family, work, neighbourhood, and formal and informal networks. It is recommended that students complete one of SOCI 100, SOCI 101, or SOCI 102 before taking this course. Restricted to students with second-year standing or above.

courses.title: Sociology and Natural Resources
courses.description: Sociological perspectives on property, resource industries (such as agriculture, fishing, forestry and mining), resource development, and resource communities. It is recommended that students complete one of SOCI 100, SOCI 101, or SOCI 102 before taking this course. Restricted to students with second-year standing or above.

courses.title: Social Inequality
courses.description: Tendencies toward equality and inequality; manifestations of inequality (occupation, education, gender, ethnicity, income, power) and their consequences; caste and class features of major stratification systems; theories of social class; stratification profile of contemporary industrial societies. It is recommended that students complete one of SOCI 100, SOCI 101, or SOCI 102 before taking this course. Restricted to students with second-year standing or above.

courses.title: Built Environments
courses.description: Physical, social, and economic aspects of built environments, including housing and community planning. It is recommended that students complete one of SOCI 100, SOCI 101, or SOCI 102 before taking this course. Restricted to students with second-year standing or above.

courses.title: Sociology of Sexualities
courses.description: Sexual identities, communities, practices, and norms across social and historical contexts. It is recommended that students complete one of SOCI 100, SOCI 101, SOCI 102 or SOCI 200 before taking this course. Restricted to students with second-year standing or above.

courses.title: Sociological Theories: Classical and Contemporary Approaches
courses.description: An examination of selected traditions, conceptual problems, and current topics in the field of sociological theory. Credit will be granted for only one of SOCI 370 or both SOCI 371, SOCI 372. Prerequisite: One of SOCI 100, SOCI 101, SOCI 102.

courses.title: Classical Traditions in Theory
courses.description: An examination of selected traditions, conceptual problems and topics in the foundational theories of sociology. Credit will be granted for only one of SOCI 371 or SOCI 370. Prerequisite: One of SOCI 100, SOCI 101, SOCI 102.

courses.title: Contemporary Directions in Theory
courses.description: A survey of theories in contemporary sociology. Credit will be granted for only one of SOCI 372 or SOCI 370. Prerequisite: One of SOCI 100, SOCI 101, SOCI 102.

courses.title: Sociological Methods: Survey Research
courses.description: Questionnaire design, interviewing, sampling, and analysis of survey data. Prerequisite: One of SOCI 100, SOCI 101, SOCI 102, SOCI 217.

prereq.text: One of SOCI 100, SOCI 101, SOCI 102, SOCI 217

courses.title: Sociological Methods: Experimental Research
courses.description: Research strategies associated with the implementation of experimental methods in sociology. Prerequisite: One of SOCI 100, SOCI 101, SOCI 102 and SOCI 217.

prereq.text: One of SOCI 100, SOCI 101, SOCI 102 and SOCI 217

courses.title: Sociological Methods: Qualitative Research
courses.description: Examination of the different traditions of qualitative sociological inquiry and the associated methodological features used to study the interpretive practices and meanings in the everyday lives of individuals. Prerequisite: One of SOCI 100, SOCI 101, SOCI 102 and SOCI 217.

prereq.text: One of SOCI 100, SOCI 101, SOCI 102 and SOCI 217

courses.title: Sociological Methods: Historical Research
courses.description: Key approaches and debates in historical research methods. Using archival sources, historical texts, and sociological arguments to?examine how the past shapes the present. Prerequisite: One of SOCI 100, SOCI 101, SOCI 102 and SOCI 217.

prereq.text: One of SOCI 100, SOCI 101, SOCI 102 and SOCI 217

courses.title: Sociology of Health and Illness
courses.description: Classic and contemporary sociological perspectives on health, illness, and health care. It is recommended that students complete one of SOCI 100, SOCI 101, or SOCI 102 before taking this course. Restricted to students with second-year standing or above.

courses.title: Drugs and Society
courses.description: Social dimensions of the causes, consequences, regulation, and treatment of substance use from Canadian and international perspectives. It is recommended that students complete one of SOCI 100, SOCI 101, or SOCI 102 before taking this course. Restricted to students with second-year standing or above.

courses.title: Selected Topics in Canadian Society
courses.description: Selected areas of study relating to Canadian society such as BC Studies; French Canada's demographic problems; rural communities; social welfare and community programs in Canada. Consult the Department for this year's offerings. It is recommended that students complete one of SOCI 100, SOCI 101, or SOCI 102 before taking this course. Restricted to students with second-year standing or above.

courses.title: Feminist Theory
courses.description: The emergence of feminist theory, its relationship to sociology, and the major theoretical schools of thought. Prerequisite: One of SOCI 100, SOCI 101, SOCI 102.

courses.title: Theories of Family and Kinship
courses.description: Theoretical approaches to the study of the family and family forms. Prerequisite: One of SOCI 100, SOCI 101, SOCI 102, SOCI 200.

prereq.text: One of SOCI 100, SOCI 101, SOCI 102, SOCI 200

courses.title: Selected Topics in Sociological Theory
courses.description: An in-depth examination of selected sociological theories. Consult the department for this year's offerings. Prerequisite: One of SOCI 100, SOCI 101, SOCI 102.

courses.title: Social Statistics II
courses.description: Primary emphasis on applications of statistical techniques to data in Sociology. It is recommended that students complete one of SOCI 100, SOCI 101, or SOCI 102 before taking this course. Restricted to students with second-year standing or above. Prerequisite: SOCI 328.

courses.title: Sociology of the Environment
courses.description: Sociological approaches to the study of environmental conflicts, issues, movements, impact of changing technology, economic development on the environment. It is recommended that students complete one of SOCI 100, SOCI 101, or SOCI 102 before taking this course. Restricted to students with second-year standing or above.

courses.title: Sociology of Food
courses.description: Cultural, economic, and political aspects of food production and consumption, including connections to class, ethnicity, and gender. Food-related social movements will be included. It is recommended that students complete one of SOCI 100, SOCI 101, or SOCI 102 before taking this course. Restricted to students with second-year standing or above.

courses.title: Urban Sociology
courses.description: Demographic, behavioural, and organizational aspects of urban structures and of urbanization in different societies and periods. It is recommended that students complete one of SOCI 100, SOCI 101, or SOCI 102 before taking this course. Restricted to students with second-year standing or above.

courses.title: Global Citizenship
courses.description: Sociology approaches to global citizenship, including its contested nature and intellectual lineage.

courses.title: Directed Studies
courses.description: General reading and/or a research undertaking, with the agreement, and under the supervision, of a Department faculty member selected by the student. It is recommended that students complete one of SOCI 100, SOCI 101, or SOCI 102 before taking this course. Restricted to students with second-year standing or above. And permission of the Department.

courses.title: International Service Learning
courses.description: International field placement normally for eight to ten weeks; pre-departure seminars (eight to twelve seminars or equivalent) with student presentation seminars upon return from the field.

courses.title: Economic Sociology
courses.description: Analysis of economic actions and institutions using the concepts and methods of sociology. It is recommended that students complete one of SOCI 100, SOCI 101, or SOCI 102 before taking this course. Restricted to students with second-year standing or above.

courses.title: Society, Economy and Family
courses.description: The study of family in social and economic contexts. It is recommended that students complete one of SOCI 100, SOCI 101, SOCI 102 or SOCI 200 before taking this course. Credit will be granted for only one of SOCI 441 and FMST 440. Equivalency: FMST 440. Restricted to students with second-year standing or above.
courses.equivalency: FMST 440. Restricted to students with second-year standing or above

courses.title: Families and Work
courses.description: The effect of combining family and work roles. It is recommended that students complete one of SOCI 100, SOCI 101, SOCI 102 or SOCI 200 before taking this course. Credit will be granted for only one of SOCI 442 and FMST 442. Equivalency: FMST 442. Restricted to students with second-year standing or above.
courses.equivalency: FMST 442. Restricted to students with second-year standing or above

courses.title: Honours Tutorial
courses.description: Requires the presentation of at least one research paper. Restricted to students in the Sociology Honours program. Prerequisite: One of SOCI 100, SOCI 101, SOCI 102.

courses.title: Political Sociology
courses.description: The social and economic bases of political power, including the study of the state, ideology, political movements, revolutions, and political violence. It is recommended that students complete one of SOCI 100, SOCI 101, or SOCI 102 before taking this course. Restricted to students with second-year standing or above.

courses.title: Social Movements
courses.description: A study of the sources, stages, and effects of social movements in developing and modernized societies. It is recommended that students complete one of SOCI 100, SOCI 101, or SOCI 102 before taking this course. Restricted to students with second-year standing or above.

courses.title: Sociology of the Arts
courses.description: An examination of the arts as social practices from the standpoint of the relationships among artists, critics, patrons, and public; and the social institutions through which these relationships are structured. It is recommended that students complete one of SOCI 100, SOCI 101, or SOCI 102 before taking this course. Restricted to students with second-year standing or above.

courses.title: Sociology of Education
courses.description: Examines the role of schooling in modern society including links with inequality, knowledge production, socialization and the economy. It is recommended that students complete one of SOCI 100, SOCI 101, or SOCI 102 before taking this course. Restricted to students with second-year standing or above.

courses.title: Queer Theory and Politics
courses.description: Empirical expressions and political possibilities of queer theory. It is recommended that students complete one of SOCI 100, SOCI 101, or SOCI 102 before taking this course. Restricted to students with second-year standing or above. Prerequisite: SOCI 369.

courses.title: Sociology of Crime and Justice
courses.description: Critical examination of specific forms of crime in relation to the criminal justice system including law, enforcement, and corrections. It is recommended that students complete one of SOCI 100, SOCI 101, or SOCI 102 before taking this course. Restricted to students with second-year standing or above.

courses.title: Sociology of Mental Illness
courses.description: A sociological approach to the meaning of mental illness; the organization of psychiatric treatment; problems in the explanation of the distribution of mental illness in a population. It is recommended that students complete one of SOCI 100, SOCI 101, or SOCI 102 before taking this course. Restricted to students with second-year standing or above.

courses.title: Sociology of Soccer
courses.description: Soccer and colonialism, soccer and global politics, and inequalities in soccer by gender, sexuality, race and class. It is recommended that students complete one of SOCI 100, SOCI 101, or SOCI 102 before taking this course. Restricted to students with second-year standing or above.

courses.title: Social Determinants of Health
courses.description: Relationships between social phenomena (e.g., personal beliefs, lifestyle practices, social support, socio-economic status, social class, gender, and ethnicity) and the health of human populations. It is recommended that students complete one of SOCI 100, SOCI 101, or SOCI 102 before taking this course. Restricted to students with second-year standing or above.

courses.title: Urban Ethnographic Field School (UEFS)
courses.description: Approximately 50 hours of volunteering and fieldwork based in community organizations with theoretical approaches to urban spaces. Students will engage in collaborative research while considering a range of theoretical and methodological approaches. Students may earn a maximum of 6 credits from ANTH 480 and SOCI 480. It is recommended that students complete one of SOCI 100, SOCI 101, or SOCI 102 before taking this course. Restricted to students with second-year standing or above.

courses.title: Contemporary Chinese Society
courses.description: Current social topics in Chinese society; perspectives on gender, inequality, culture, and social relations. It is recommended that students complete one of SOCI 100, SOCI 101, or SOCI 102 before taking this course. Restricted to students with second-year standing or above.

courses.title: Advanced Studies in Sociology
courses.description: An intensive examination of selected topics in Sociology. Consult the department for this year's offerings. It is recommended that students complete one of SOCI 100, SOCI 101, or SOCI 102 before taking this course. Restricted to students with second-year standing or above.
